facts.raw_span: a 1½-week history of headache and blurred vision
MRI of the brain demonstrated a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
an HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL
Serum toxoplasma IgG was elevated
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes)
positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii (286 copies/mL)
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
fever to 39.6 °C
generalized weakness
a 1-day history of productive cough
Chest radiograph showed a new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence

The patient has a new left upper lobe opacification, diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence, and a low CD4 count, which are all consistent with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
The patient has a CD4 count <20 cells/µL and an HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL, which are both indicative of HIV-associated immunodeficiency.

The patient has a low CD4 count and multiple infections, including toxoplasmosis and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, which are all consistent with opportunistic infections.

The patient has a low CD4 count, multiple infections, and a recent initiation of antiretroviral therapy, which are all consistent with immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome.

rationales.F01: Headache and blurred vision are common symptoms of cerebral toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F02: Ring-enhancing lesion in the brain is a characteristic finding of cerebral toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F03: HIV infection with low CD4 count increases the risk of opportunistic infections, including toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F05: Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG indicates past or current infection with Toxoplasma gondii.
rationales.F07: Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF confirm the diagnosis of cerebral toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F08: Histopathologic examination of brain tissue revealing bradyzoites and tachyzoites is diagnostic of toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F09: Fever is a non-specific symptom that can be associated with various infections, including opportunistic infections in HIV-positive patients.
rationales.F11: Productive cough is a symptom that can be associated with various respiratory infections, including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
rationales.F12: Chest radiograph showing new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence is suggestive of an opportunistic infection, such as Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
